topic: Disney names Adobe its Official AI Innovation Partner: private Firefly Foundry models trained on Disney IP (9 Nov 2026, Adobe MAX)
instagram_caption:
Disney is training AI on its own characters.

On 9 November, Disney named Adobe its "Official AI Innovation Partner" in a multi-year deal announced at Adobe MAX. Adobe will use Firefly Foundry to build private models trained on Disney's characters, environments and visual styles. Disney's Imagineering team already uses two of them, one to turn hand-drawn sketches into concept art. Financial terms weren't disclosed.

Why it matters: the biggest brands aren't using generic AI for brand work. They're training private models on what they already own, so the output stays on-brand and commercially safe. Your brand library is about to become your most useful AI asset.

What to do this week:
1. Audit your brand assets. Gather approved logos, product shots, colours and past campaigns in one place, with usage rights clear.
2. Write down what makes your visuals yours: tone, palette, composition and what's off-limits.
3. Check what your AI tools do with your uploads, and whether outputs are cleared for commercial use.

Generic AI makes generic brands. Train it on what only you have.

linkedin_text:
Disney is training AI on its own characters.

On 9 November at Adobe MAX, Disney named Adobe its Official AI Innovation Partner in a multi-year deal. Adobe will use Firefly Foundry to build private generative models trained on Disney's characters, environments and visual styles, with what Adobe calls commercially safe, production-ready output. Walt Disney Imagineering already uses two such models, one of which turns hand-drawn sketches into concept art. The deal also covers Walt Disney Studios' StudioLAB and ESPN. Financial terms were not disclosed.

Our take: the most valuable brand in entertainment isn't relying on generic AI for brand work. It is training private models on what it already owns. For marketers, that shifts the question from "which AI tool?" to "how good is our brand library?"

Three moves for this week:
1. Audit your brand assets. Put approved logos, product shots, palettes and past campaigns in one place, with usage rights clear.
2. Write down what makes your visuals yours: tone, composition, and what is off-limits.
3. Check what your AI tools do with your uploads, and whether outputs are cleared for commercial use.

Generic AI makes generic brands. Train it on what only you have.
